repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#Stop_Button).button_button != "pushed")
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Stop_Button).button_button == "pushed")
all(#Switch).switch_off()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait on 'Button.Button == "pushed"'. The candidate polls the condition at the start of the 1000ms period. F1 shows the input changed to 'pushed' at t=0 and held for 100ms. F2 confirms the IR acted at t=100ms while the candidate did nothing because its `if` guard evaluated to false at t=0. The candidate must block on the rising edge rather than sampling it periodically.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking `wait until` for the rising edge, followed by the action and the state update. This ensures the action fires exactly when the condition transitions from false to true, matching the IR's `wait(..., edge rising)` semantics.
